content.title: Artemis III - NASA
content.text: NASA's Artemis III mission in low Earth orbit will test integrated operations between the Orion spacecraft and one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin respectively. Spaceport The systems and facilities that assemble and launch NASA's rockets and spacecraft for NASA’s Artemis missions. Learn More about Spaceport Crew Launch The Artemis III crew will launch in Orion on the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Learn More about Crew Launch Spacecraft The crew of Artemis III will ride to Earth orbit aboard the Orion spacecraft, where the crew will test rendezvous and docking capabilities between Orion and private commercial spacecraft needed to land astronauts on the Moon. This test will take place with one or both providers. Learn More about Spacecraft Human Landing Systems NASA's Artemis III demonstration mission in low Earth orbit will test one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin respectively. The mission will launch crew in the Orion spacecraft on top of the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket to test rendezvous and docking capabilities between Orion and the private commercial spacecraft needed to land astronauts on the Moon.
